findings.title: Compute the `queued` default per instance, not once at import
Make `to_dict()` output JSON-serializable for task kwargs
Avoid silently losing cycle protection when the source dict fails to parse
Check subclass `should_sync` overrides for the new parameter

response:
## 1) Severity: HIGH | Type: Bug
Title: Compute the `queued` default per instance, not once at import

Affected:
- src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:18

Explanation:
`queued: datetime = timezone.now()` runs once, when the class is defined at module import. Every `AssignmentSource` created without an explicit `queued` gets the same timestamp: the process start time, not the time the assignment was queued. Any later logic that relies on `queued` (staleness checks, ordering, debugging) will be silently wrong. `test_to_dict` only checks that `queued` is not None, so it cannot catch this.

Proposed fix:
~~~python
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AssignmentSource:
    source_name: str
    integration_id: int
    queued: datetime = field(default_factory=timezone.now)
~~~

## 2) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Make `to_dict()` output JSON-serializable for task kwargs

Affected:
- src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:27-28
- src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py:137-144

Explanation:
`asdict(self)` returns a raw `datetime` for `queued`. That dict is passed as a Celery task kwarg. The commit history says the intent is to pass JSON-safe data, but a `datetime` is not JSON-serializable. With a JSON task serializer, enqueueing either fails or relies on serializer-specific coercion.

On the consumer side, `from_dict` does `cls(**input_dict)` with no type conversion. A round-tripped `queued` would therefore arrive as a string (or another non-`datetime` type) and the object would have the wrong type.

Fix:
- Serialize `queued` explicitly, for example as ISO 8601.
- Parse it back in `from_dict`.
- Add a test that round-trips the dict through `json.dumps`/`json.loads`.

Proposed fix:
~~~python
def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
    d = asdict(self)
    d["queued"] = self.queued.isoformat()
    return d

@classmethod
def from_dict(cls, input_dict: dict[str, Any]) -> AssignmentSource | None:
    try:
        data = dict(input_dict)
        if isinstance(data.get("queued"), str):
            data["queued"] = datetime.fromisoformat(data["queued"])
        return cls(**data)
    except (ValueError, TypeError):
        return None
~~~

## 3) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Update the `sync_assignee_outbound` signature, not `sync_status_outbound`

Affected:
- src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:410-418
- src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py:59-61

Explanation:
The task now calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source)`. However, the abstract signature that was changed is `sync_status_outbound`, and nothing in this diff passes `assignment_source` to that method. Meanwhile the abstract `sync_assignee_outbound` contract was left unchanged.

Any concrete integration whose `sync_assignee_outbound` does not accept `**kwargs` or an `assignment_source` parameter will raise `TypeError` inside the task, and outbound assignee sync will break. I can't see the implementations in this diff, so please verify that each one (Jira, Jira Server, GitHub, GitLab, VSTS, example, etc.) accepts the new kwarg.

Proposed fix:
~~~python
@abstractmethod
def sync_assignee_outbound(
    self,
    external_issue,
    user,
    assign=True,
    assignment_source: AssignmentSource | None = None,
    **kwargs,
):
    ...

# and revert the unused assignment_source param on sync_status_outbound
~~~

## 4) Severity: LOW | Type: Bug
Title: Avoid silently losing cycle protection when the source dict fails to parse

Affected:
- src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:30-35
- src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py:53-56

Explanation:
If `assignment_source_dict` is present but malformed, `from_dict` returns `None` with no logging. `should_sync` then treats the assignment as having no source and syncs back to the originating integration. That recreates the exact sync cycle this PR is meant to break, and leaves no trace of why. Malformed input could come from a version skew between producer and consumer, or from extra keys.

Fix:
- Log a warning when parsing fails.
- Consider ignoring unknown keys so that adding fields later stays backward compatible.

Proposed fix:
~~~python
except (ValueError, TypeError):
    logger.warning("assignment_source.parse_failed", extra={"input": input_dict})
    return None
~~~

## 5) Severity: LOW | Type: Maintainability
Title: Check subclass `should_sync` overrides for the new parameter

Affected:
- src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:66, 382

Explanation:
The task now calls `installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)` with a second positional argument. Any integration subclass that overrides `should_sync(self, attribute)` with the old one-argument signature will raise `TypeError`. I can't see whether such overrides exist from this diff, so please search for them.

Proposed fix:
~~~text
grep -rn "def should_sync" src/sentry/integrations
# Update any override to: def should_sync(self, attribute, sync_source=None)
~~~
